quiz.title: Data Storage and File Formats
quiz.description: How data is stored and represented: CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, object storage, and the trade-offs between row- and column-oriented formats.

questions.question_text: Which file format stores data as comma-separated plain text rows?
What type of storage format is Apache Parquet?
Why are columnar formats like Parquet often preferred for analytical queries?
questions.option_a: They let queries read only the columns needed, reducing I/O
questions.option_b: They are the only format Python can read
questions.correct_answer: They let queries read only the columns needed, reducing I/O

questions.question_text: What does 'schema-on-read' mean, as commonly applied to data lakes?
questions.option_a: The structure of the data is interpreted when it is read, not enforced when it is written
questions.option_b: Data must be validated before every write
questions.option_c: Data cannot be changed once written
questions.option_d: Schemas are stored as CSV files
questions.correct_answer: The structure of the data is interpreted when it is read, not enforced when it is written

questions.question_text: Which of these is an example of an object storage service?
What is a key benefit of storing data in Avro format for streaming pipelines?
questions.option_a: It embeds a schema with the data, supporting schema evolution
questions.option_b: It cannot be used with Kafka
questions.correct_answer: It embeds a schema with the data, supporting schema evolution

questions.question_text: In a data lake architecture, raw, unprocessed data is often referred to as which layer?
Which compression consideration is most relevant when choosing a file format for large-scale storage?
questions.option_a: Balancing compression ratio against read/write speed
questions.option_b: Whether the file can be opened in Notepad
questions.option_d: The color of the file icon
questions.correct_answer: Balancing compression ratio against read/write speed

questions.option_a: A centralized repository that stores raw structured and unstructured data at scale
questions.option_b: A single table in a relational database
questions.correct_answer: A centralized repository that stores raw structured and unstructured data at scale

questions.question_text: Which format is typically preferred for row-by-row transactional writes rather than analytical scans?
questions.option_a: Row-based formats like CSV or JSON
questions.correct_answer: Row-based formats like CSV or JSON

questions.question_text: What does 'partitioning' a dataset in storage (e.g., by date) primarily help with?
questions.option_a: Improving query performance by letting engines skip irrelevant partitions
questions.correct_answer: Improving query performance by letting engines skip irrelevant partitions

questions.question_text: What is a common downside of storing data only as JSON at very large scale?
questions.option_a: It is verbose and less efficient to scan than binary columnar formats
questions.option_c: It cannot be parsed by any tool
questions.option_d: It is a row-oriented binary format
questions.correct_answer: It is verbose and less efficient to scan than binary columnar formats
